title: claim --resume takes back the same actor's held bead from another machine
description:
A developer cannot move an in-progress bead from laptop to desktop. Ownership is per run (one worktree on one machine), so the desktop's bops claim is refused (assigned to the same actor) or lost; claim --resume only accepts state=landing (internal/intent/ownership.go ClaimResume, the ref.State != StateLanding case). The only routes are release on the laptop (scope/abandoned add bops:hold, hiding the bead from next for 120 min, and need the laptop) or claim --force after stale_minutes. MULTI-DEV-PLAN §5 and PROCESS §0 promise machine-hopping works with a note and bd sync.

Fix: (1) the claim ref message gains machine=<hostname> (internal/lock/message.go; ParseMessage ignores unknown keys, so older bops reads new refs fine). (2) ClaimResume also accepts state=held when ref.Actor equals this run's actor AND ref.Machine is set AND differs from this machine; it replaces the ref under a lease on the sha it read, writing this run and state=held, then does finishTakeover with resumed=<old-run>. (3) Same machine is refused (sibling worktrees and /bead-loop subagents share the actor; stranded holds already cover a dead worktree). A ref with no machine key (older bops) is refused with the fix: release on the original machine, or wait and use --force. (4) The old machine finds out the way a forced takeover does: lost_claims on its next sync; note/land/release return lost, with text kept at saved_to.

Open owner decision: SPEC §1.9 bumps the contract on any change to exit semantics or state conventions. This changes what --resume accepts and adds a ref key. Either bump to contract 2, or rule it additive (a held bead was refused before and is now claimed; no output field changes).
acceptance_criteria: From machine B, claim --resume on a bead held by the same actor on machine A returns claimed, exit 0, and the ref names B's run with machine=B. A's next sync lists the bead in lost_claims, and A's note returns lost with saved_to. It is refused (exit 3) for another actor, for the same machine, and for a ref with no machine key. Two concurrent resumes from B and C have one winner. Replica tests cover each case. SPEC §3.0/§3.2, PROCESS §2 and §12 and MULTI-DEV-PLAN §5 document a machine switch as: push the branch, bops note with NEXT, then claim --resume on the other machine. The generated skill keeps --resume out of autonomous loops.

title: note/renew can turn an interrupted done release's landing ref back into a held claim
description: A bops release --reason done that is killed after verifyHold replaces the ref with state=landing and before it marks the hold (SetReleaseOwed) leaves a hold that is not Given, has no Intended, and matches the live landing ref. bops sync now finishes such a hold as a done release, but note and renew (lockHeld -> refreshRef) call Lock.Replace(entry.SHA, StateHeld) without reading the ref's state, which turns the landing back into a held claim. checkHold uses Lock.Live (sha only). Fix: have refreshRef/checkHold read the ref state and, for a landing ref on an unmarked hold, mark it owed and finish it via settleRelease instead of refreshing. Test: Replace the ref to landing directly after a claim, then bops note; the ref must stay landing.
notes: Same unmarked landing hold also slips past sweep from this clone: sweepOne's finishRelease ignores a hold that is not Given, so sweep deletes the landing ref and closes the bead with the claim display still shown, and the next sync reports it lost. Fix both by marking an unmarked hold whose live ref is landing as owed inside settleReleaseAs (one place every caller reaches), as syncHold now does.

bops:note run=01M8FQFXB68RKV2T57KSJG09N5 op=d-bcfc52a2958a34d2
Ahead/behind surface on bd 1.3.4 (verified in an isolated scratch: bare git+file remote, two clones, own XDG dirs; never the real ledger):
- `bd sql`: "not yet supported in embedded mode". `bd vc status --json`: branch and commit only. `bd branch`: local branches only.
- `bd diff HEAD origin/main --json`: issue-row fields only. A label-only or comment-only commit reads "No changes between HEAD and origin/main" (plain text, not JSON, even with --json). So it misses a note and a claim's comment; not usable as "ahead".
- `bd federation status --json`: per Dolt remote, Status.LocalAhead / LocalBehind (commit counts), Reachable, ReachError, plus top-level pendingChanges (uncommitted working-set rows). Counts label-only and comment-only commits (ahead 1), an uncommitted write (pendingChanges 1), and a pulled merge (ahead 2 until pushed). No Dolt remote: peers []. Exit 0 in every case.
Freshness: it fetches from each remote first (0.3-0.5 s on a local remote), so with Reachable true the counts are as of that call. With the remote unreachable it still exits 0, Reachable false, ReachError set, and the counts are against the remote-tracking branch as of the last successful pull or fetch. The fetch updates the remote-tracking branch only (no merge).
KEY DECISION: status and doctor use `bd federation status --json` (one call, bounded by a timeout), report ahead>0 as unpublished, ahead>0 and behind>0 as diverged, pendingChanges>0 as uncommitted, and say when the counts are from the last fetch because the remote did not answer.

description: refreshRef always replaces the claim ref with state held. title: bops: PreToolUse hook that refuses raw claims on a bops ledger
description:
Rules such as "never `bd update --claim` or `bd reclaim` on a bops ledger" are repeated in CLAUDE.md, skills and memory, and an agent under context pressure can still forget them. bops already installs a SessionStart hook.

Prior art: dibs installs a PreToolUse hook that blocks an edit to a file another agent claimed (exit 2, naming the holder) and fails open if dibs itself fails; its author notes that protocol adherence that relies on the model remembering degrades under context pressure (https://github.com/polymatx/dibs).

Proposal: an opt-in PreToolUse hook that inspects Bash commands for `bd update ... --claim` and `bd reclaim` and refuses them with "use bops claim / bops claim --force". Fail open on any hook error.

title: bops renew: extend a claim's lease without posting a comment

Proposal: `bops renew <id> [<id>...]`: update the lock ref (and its age) for each bead held by this run, no ledger write, JSON outcome per bead. `note` keeps its current behaviour.

title: session-start in another session can drop an in-flight claim's journal entry and orphan its lock ref
description:
Found reviewing development-collaboration-zp93 (bops-fhv dogfood).

If a session starts in any worktree of a clone while the /bead-loop orchestrator is mid bops claim (journal Intended set or PhasePushing, and the hook's fetch predates the push), lock.Settle takes the PhasePushing → Abandon path or reads the hold as Displaced or lost; Sync's lost path then Journal.Drop + clearOwnDisplay. If the orchestrator's create-only push then succeeds, the ref exists on origin with no journal entry and the ledger display may be cleared: an orphan ref or an untrackable hold. The runstate file lock (Store.update) protects each write, not the read-settle-write sequence across processes. Opening a second Claude session during a loop is routine. Needs a repro and a cross-process guard (hold the runstate lock across settle, or skip holds in Intended/PhasePushing owned by a live process).

title: Run the bops v0.2.0 android/arm64 release binary on Termux
description:
bops-ss6.14's acceptance criteria require the binary to run on Termux arm64, and nobody has checked that. CI and Docker ran only the linux amd64 and arm64 builds. The android/arm64 build is a PIE that uses /system/bin/linker64. It is built with CGO_ENABLED=0, so DNS goes through Go's resolver; on Android that can't read /etc/resolv.conf, which may affect anything that needs the network (claim, sync, land).

This needs a person with the device, so it carries needs-human.

Steps: follow the download block in bops/README.md with t=android_arm64 and install into $PREFIX/bin. Run bops version, then bops doctor and bops next in a clone of a bops ledger. If DNS fails, try the linux_arm64 build too; it is static and also runs on Termux.

REF: https://github.com/extremenelson/beads-ops/releases/tag/bops/v0.2.0, bops-ss6.14
acceptance_criteria: On a Termux arm64 device, bops_v0.2.0_android_arm64.tar.gz from the bops/v0.2.0 release verifies against checksums.txt and installs to $PREFIX/bin, and bops version prints bops=v0.2.0 and contract=1 and finds bd. Ledger commands (doctor, next and the rest) are out of scope natively: bd 1.3.4 has no Termux build that opens an embedded ledger (android_arm64 is cgo-free, linux_arm64 needs glibc), so on Termux they need proot-distro with the linux_arm64 builds until bd ships an android build with cgo. That limit is recorded where Termux users will see it.

title: Flaky replicas CI: bd dolt pull fails on a packfile with no index in Dolt's git-remote-cache
description: The replicas job (BOPS_INTEGRATION=1, bd 1.3.4, ubuntu-latest) intermittently fails TestReplicaRaceSharedActor in bops/cmd/bops/replica_test.go. Both 40-trial claim races pass; the failure is the post-race reconciliation loop (replica_test.go ~line 325: for r in a, b, a { r.bops("sync") }), where bops sync's bd dolt pull exits 1 with: 'Error: fetch from origin/main: Error 1105: git cat-file -s parse error ("error: packfile <tmp>/a/.beads/embeddeddolt/it/.dolt/git-remote-cache/<hash>/repo.git/objects/pack/pack-<sha>.pack index unavailable\n321"): strconv.ParseInt: parsing ... invalid syntax'. So Dolt's git remote cache had a .pack with no .idx (likely a concurrent or interrupted fetch into the shared cache), and Dolt then misparsed git's stderr as the object size. Seen twice in the last 40 bops.yml runs: 43091094440 (2026-11-11, plan/bops-v0.1.0-ceo-review, push) and 43470722709 (2026-11-13, work/bops-oy9.1 @ c17e25f, push; the pull_request run of the same commit passed). Not caused by either PR's diff. Investigate: (1) does it reproduce locally with BOPS_RACE_TRIALS raised and two replicas pulling at once; (2) is the cache shared between replicas a and b or between bd processes of one replica racing; (3) whether bops sync should classify this error and retry once like the dolt lock retry (withLockRetry/isLockError in internal/intent/intent.go), or the test should serialize syncs; (4) file upstream with gastownhall/beads or dolthub/dolt if it is a bd/Dolt cache race. Do not mask it by blanket-retrying every bd error.
acceptance_criteria: Root cause written on the bead (bops, test harness, or upstream bd/Dolt) with a reproduction or the evidence that rules each out; the fix (a narrowly classified retry in sync, a test change, or an upstream issue link plus a documented, narrowly matched retry) lands with a test that fails without it; the replicas job passes TestReplicaRaceSharedActor on 10 consecutive runs (gh workflow run or BOPS_RACE_TRIALS loop).

comments.author: Alex Nelson
comments.text:
bops:note run=01M7AZZ0G4E63CRF1F1JV8B4WR
Investigation so far (no code changed yet).

Ruled out: a killed bd call. bdx.Exec uses exec.CommandContext, so a deadline would SIGKILL bd mid-fetch and could orphan a .pack, but in the failing run claims took p50 3.0s, max 5.7s against a 60s budget. Replicas a and b are separate clones with separate Dolt caches, and the harness runs one bops process per replica at a time.

Mechanism found (GIT_TRACE on bd 1.3.4, git 2.56.1): every bd dolt pull fetches into .beads/embeddeddolt/<db>/.dolt/git-remote-cache/<hash>/repo.git and git then runs `git maintenance run --auto --detach`, which ran `git repack -d -l --cruft --cruft-expiration=2.weeks.ago --write-midx` in a detached process on 8 of 8 pulls. -d deletes old packs. A pull then makes ~150 `git cat-file -s` calls on that cache. 'packfile ... index unavailable' is git's message when a pack's .idx vanishes under a reader, and Dolt parses that stderr as the size (the strconv.ParseInt error). The failure sits at the post-race `sync a, b, a`, the first point where pulls on one replica run back to back.

Not reproduced: macOS git 2.56.1, 75 back-to-back pulls (0 failures, with and without maintenance.autoDetach=false); a direct loop of that repack against 5100 cat-file -s reads in the same cache (0 bad outputs); Ubuntu 24.04 container, git 2.43.0, bd 1.3.4 linux_arm64 checksum-verified, 120 pulls each way (0 failures). CI's ubuntu-latest runner ships a newer git than 2.43 and amd64.

KEY DECISION: pending the owner, between (a) running the real replica suite in a container that matches CI's git, (b) a test-only mitigation (maintenance.autoDetach=false in the replica env) verified by 10 CI runs, (c) an upstream report to dolthub/dolt with this evidence.

comments.author: Alex Nelson
comments.text:
TRIAGE 2026-11-13 (host A). Confirmed in code at 3963f80, and worse than filed: a landing with no land record is invisible, not just stuck.
- ReleaseWithText (internal/intent/ownership.go:878) never reads the landed records; reason done only flips the ref to state=landing (verifyHold -> Lock.Replace, :984) and adds bops:landing (:1024).
- Sweep (internal/intent/intent.go:559) does `if len(landed) == 0 { continue }`: such a bead is not closed, and not listed in pending or unknown either.
- Stale (internal/intent/stale.go:58): a landing ref is "neither stale nor an orphan", so stale never lists it.
- next excludes bops:landing. So nothing reports it; only a person who knows the id runs claim --resume as the holder (PROCESS §12, abandoned landing).
Realistic trigger in the loop: bops land fails (non-URL ref as in step 3, a --verify mismatch, network) and the agent goes on to release --reason done, as the skill orders them.

RECOMMENDATION: refuse, not warn. A warning lands in JSON nobody reads, and the result is silent. release --reason done with no landed record -> exit 3, outcome refused, reason "no land record: run bops land <id> --ref <pr-url> first, or release with --reason scope"; check before the ref is touched; same rule with lock.mode none. Defence in depth: sweep lists a bops:landing bead with no landed record under unknown instead of skipping it. Contract change: commands.json release preconditions, SPEC §2 (release/landing rows), docs/COMMANDS.md regen, golden.

KEY DECISION (owner): refuse (recommended) or warn. Raised to P2: it can strand loop work silently.

title: lock.Exec timeout does not bound ssh: one git call hung 241s past its 20s deadline
description: Found on host B during T13 step 0 (2026-11-12). lock.Exec.Run uses exec.CommandContext with callTimeout 20s. When the ssh connection stalls, the context kills git, but git's ssh child keeps the stdout/stderr pipes open. cmd.Run then waits for EOF until ssh's ServerAliveInterval*CountMax expires (180s here), so bops doctor took 241s and reported 'signal: killed: Timeout, server github.com not responding'. Fix: set cmd.WaitDelay (Go 1.20+) and/or put git in its own process group and kill the group; also consider adding -o ConnectTimeout=10 next to BatchMode in sshCommand.
acceptance_criteria: With an ssh that hangs (test seam or a fake ssh that sleeps), Exec.Run returns within callTimeout plus a small WaitDelay; a unit test covers it.

comments.author: Alex Nelson
comments.text:
bops:note run=01M79EFY2K0QNPB3QV2EYZHEMF
Fix in place on work/bops-ss6.27. Exec.Run sets cmd.WaitDelay=2s, so once the 20s deadline kills git, Run stops waiting on pipes still held by git's ssh child. sshCommand also adds -o ConnectTimeout=10, unless one is already set, next to BatchMode. The new test TestExecRunBoundedByWaitDelay uses a fake git that leaves a grandchild holding stdout: it takes 30s without the fix and 2.2s with it. gofmt, vet, go test ./... and the docs diff all pass.

KEY DECISION: no process-group kill. bops has no signal handling, so putting git in its own group would stop Ctrl-C from reaching it. The orphaned ssh still exits on its own ServerAlive timeout, but it no longer blocks bops.

title: min_bops refuses the read-only MCP previews of reap, gc and sweep
description: minBopsGate (bops/cmd/bops/minbops.go) refuses every command whose manifest kind is not read when the running bops is older than min_bops. reap, gc and sweep are kind write, so their dry runs, which write nothing, are refused with too_old. serve-mcp now serves those dry runs read-only (readOnlyHint true, without --enable-writes), so a read-only tool fails as a refused write while stale, next and status only warn. Fails closed; usability only. Fix: treat a preview-only command run with --dry-run=true (the default) as a read in the gate, or document the refusal.

title: Let bops sweep take --only so a person runs the preview an agent showed
description: Agents only preview sweep (MCP and skill), handing a person bops sweep --dry-run=false. The preview skips bd dolt pull and reads the local ledger, while the real run pulls and closes every merged landed bead it then finds, so the person approves an unscoped run, not the would_close list they saw. reap and gc pin their scope with --only (reap <id>@<run>). The real sweep re-checks merge state and the bead under the bead lock, so a wrong close is unlikely; this is about the approval matching the preview. Decide whether sweep gets --only (comma-separated ids from would_close; empty list a usage error; one no longer closable listed under pending) and gen.RealRun names it.

title: bops sync: finish a pending claim-ref delete even when the ledger pull stops on ledger_conflict
description: A plain claim whose pull stops on ledger_conflict deletes the ref it just created. If that delete fails, the hold is left DeletePending and the claim ref keeps the bead held for every machine. bops sync pulls before it settles holds (syncAs returns on the pull error), so on a stuck clone it cannot finish the delete until a person resolves the conflict; a ref delete needs only git. Consider settling DeletePending holds before, or regardless of, the ledger pull. Related: a claim on a clone whose ledger-conflict.json record is current still creates the ref and then gives it back; a pre-check before the ref push would avoid the spurious lost answers other machines can see in that window, but a record left after a person resolved the conflict with raw bd would then refuse claims until bops sync clears it.
acceptance_criteria: On a clone whose pull stops on ledger_conflict, bops sync deletes a DeletePending claim ref and still reports ledger_conflict; tested with the fake bd's operator-resolution error and the deleteFails git fixture.

title: bops claim --resume and lock-off claim: decide behaviour when the ledger pull stops on ledger_conflict
description: A plain claim under lock.mode ref now gives its new ref back and fails with ledger_conflict when its pull stops on a merge conflict needing a person, as claim --force does. Two sibling paths still only warn 'ledger not pulled' and write the display locally on a stuck ledger: claim --resume (ClaimResume in bops/internal/intent/ownership.go, which has already replaced the ref, so it cannot simply give it back), and a plain claim under lock.mode none (claimLedger via pullUnlessUnpublished, which runs bd update --claim and then a push that will fail). Decide for each: fail with ledger_conflict before writing (and for resume, whether to restore the ref's previous state), or keep the warning.
acceptance_criteria: Each path does what the decision says when its pull stops on ledger_conflict, with a test using the fake bd's bd 1.3.4 operator-resolution error (stuckAfter in conflict_test.go).

title: bops reap/gc/stale: terminal id lists print ledger or ref ids that fail lock.ValidateID unquoted
description: printKV prints reap's would_release=, kept=, skipped=, failed= (and gc/stale lists) as comma-joined ids passed only through cleanText, which keeps ; | $ and backticks. A comma list is exactly the --only shape, so a person copying it gets raw ledger text and, for valid ids, drops the run pins reapDetails now offers. reapDetails single-quotes an invalid id POSIX-style ('\'' escape), which is not inert in fish (backslash escapes inside single quotes). Fix: have printKV print reap's would_release from each entry's only (omitting entries without one), or leave those lists to reapDetails; render any id failing lock.ValidateID in a non-copyable form (e.g. <invalid id %q> or hex) everywhere, replacing the POSIX quoting.
acceptance_criteria: No terminal output of reap, gc or stale prints an id failing lock.ValidateID as a bare or shell-quoted token; reap's would_release= list carries the pins; tests cover an id with shell metacharacters and a backslash.

title: bops gc: do not offer a ref-derived id that is not a valid bead id as a pastable --only entry
description: bops gc's preview lists would_delete refs by the id taken from the claim ref name (lock.Seen trims refs/bops/claims/ without lock.ValidateID). git allows ; $ backticks | ( ) in ref names, so a ref pushed by anyone with push access to the lock remote can carry shell metacharacters, and agents are told to hand a person 'bops gc --dry-run=false --only <id>' built from the preview. gc --only refuses an invalid id, but only after the shell expanded the pasted line. Apply the same treatment reap's preview now has: list such a ref with a note and offer nothing to paste (or skip it with a warning).
acceptance_criteria: A gc preview never offers an id failing lock.ValidateID as an --only entry; tests cover a ref name with shell metacharacters.

title: Finishing a pending release --reason done re-adds bops:landing to a bead closed by hand
description: settleReleaseAs checks for a closed bead only when the landing ref is gone. If a person closes the bead with bd close while the landing ref remains, finishDone still writes the release display, adding bops:landing to the closed bead, and sweep (stillLanding requires in_progress) never removes it. Fix: in finishDone, when the bead is closed, skip the display, push and drop the hold.

title: A finished release --reason done of a stranded hold loses its op and text, and its repeat answers refused
description: When a run releases (done) a hold stranded by a removed worktree and the display write fails, finishDone later writes the display under holdRun (the stranded run) with the op of a release without text, discarding the releasing run's op and text. A repeat of the same release by the releasing run then matches neither replayRelease(op) nor replayFinishedDone (which derives the plain op for e.Run.ID), and answers refused although its release landed; the text stays only in saved_to. Fix: record the releasing run (and op) when the hold is marked owed, so finishDone writes as that run with that op; this needs a state field, so weigh it against a stateVersion bump.

title: lock-off sync drops a pending release hold without writing its owed display
description: syncHold under lock.mode none drops every hold whose Entry.Given() is set. A hold from a lock.mode ref release --reason done whose display is still owed (release_pending with ledger_pending) loses that display if the repo then switches to lock.mode none, and the ledger, which is the only lock in that mode, keeps showing the claim. Rare (needs a mode change while such a hold is pending). Before dropping a Given hold with ledger_pending, write the owed release display.

title: session-start lists a pending release of a removed worktree as a stranded hold
description: syncAs with ownOnly (session-start) appends other runs' stranded holds to StrandedHolds without checking Entry.Given(). A release still pending its ledger push or display (reap's, or now a release --reason done whose write or push failed) is usually followed by removing its worktree, so it shows as a stranded hold, whose guidance is to release it from any worktree or claim --force it. Neither is right for a landing. Only a full bops sync finishes it. Report Given holds separately (for example pending_releases) with bops sync as the next step, and leave them out of StrandedHolds.

title: A pending release blocks note, land and claim --resume on the bead while the ledger cannot be pushed
description: finishRelease runs at the start of note, land, claim, claim --resume and release, and now also finishes a pending release --reason done (as it already did for a reap's pending release): it pushes the ledger and fails the command when that push fails. Under a ledger conflict that needs a person, or a down remote, bops land (for example to correct the PR) and claim --resume on that landing bead fail until the push lands, though the claim ref, which decides ownership, is fine. Decide whether a pending release's finish should be best effort in commands other than sync and release (warn and go on), and what those commands should then do with a hold that is Given.

title: bops gc: tell a closed bead's past landing evidence from live work
description: gc now reads reap's work evidence before deleting a closed bead's ref written after the bead's last ledger change (a reopened bead's claim whose ledger write has not arrived). A landed bead keeps its evidence for good (Landed() MR refs, MR URLs in notes, a merged forge MR, often its branch), so such a ref — e.g. one renewed after close, or written by a machine whose clock runs ahead of the closer's — is kept on every gc run until a lead deletes it by hand. Decide whether, for a closed bead, only evidence newer than the bead's close should count (a new branch, an open MR, a live hold), or merged MRs and Landed() refs should be excluded. Related: reap's and gc's manifests say a forge full page (ErrIncomplete) warns naming --forge none, but forgeSearch does not set unanswered for it, so no warning is printed.
acceptance_criteria: A closed bead whose only evidence predates its close (merged MR, landed ref) does not keep its ref; open MR / new branch / live hold still keep it; tests for both. Manifest text for the full-page forge case matches behaviour.

comments.author: Alex Nelson

Fixing the permanent keep here largely removes this; otherwise cap forge searches per run or rotate the start.

title: bops: replica test for a retried push keeping same-row merged labels
description: The commit-before-push fix in pushLedger is covered only through the fake bd (a commit runs straight before each push). Add a BOPS_INTEGRATION replica test in bops/cmd/bops/replica_test.go against real bd: clones A and B share a bead; A adds a label and pushes; B adds its own label to the same bead and runs bops sync, whose first push is rejected so pushLedger pulls and retries; a fresh clone C pulls and must see both labels. Confirm it fails with the commit step removed.

title: bops: pushLedger retries the commit without a pull after a failed commit
description: In pushLedger (bops/internal/intent/ownership.go) each retry runs bd dolt pull before its commit and push, even when the previous try failed at its commit and pushed nothing, so there is no rejected push to resolve. If bd 1.3.4 refuses a pull over the uncommitted rows a same-row auto-merge leaves behind, one failed commit on try 0 turns tries 1-4 into pull failures and the commit is never retried. The error still names the commit failure (it is joined into the final error), so nothing is hidden or lost, and bops sync retries. Check whether bd 1.3.4 refuses that pull; if it does, skip the retry pull after a commit failure (and drop the join it makes unreachable).
acceptance_criteria: Either a measurement showing bd 1.3.4 pulls over that working set, recorded in the research doc, or pushLedger skips the retry pull after a failed commit, with a test showing commit retried without a pull.

A bd dolt pull/push failure against a remote URL carrying credentials (git+https://user:token@...) could put the token in JSON output, MCP tool results or events. Found while reviewing the commit-before-push change, which makes pushLedger's error carry more text.
acceptance_criteria: Every warning or event detail that quotes a bd or git error goes through lock.Scrub; a test feeds an error containing a credentialed URL through a claim with a failing ledger push and checks the warning is scrubbed.

title: bops: a ledger push now publishes the whole working set, batch auto-commit work included
description: Every bops ledger push now runs bd dolt commit first, which commits the whole Dolt working set of the clone's store. With bd's dolt auto-commit set to batch (or off), a person's or another process's uncommitted bd writes on other beads are committed under an auto-generated message and published by any bops write (claim, note's pending release, release, land, sweep, sync), and a half-finished multi-step write of another bops process on this store can be published between its steps. Under the default auto-commit=on each bd write commits itself, so nothing changes there. Decide: detect batch/off mode (bd config) and warn in doctor, refuse, or document that bops requires auto-commit on.
acceptance_criteria: bops either reports (doctor warning) or documents its auto-commit requirement, with a test for the detection if one is added.

Restrict pinnable runs to a conservative charset (e.g. [A-Za-z0-9._:-]; bops runs are ULIDs), falling back to the bare id otherwise, or shell-quote the --only value in the printed form; and have the hint say what to do for a claim with no pinnable run (empty or -).

title: bops reap: forge search misreads SSH host aliases, nested GitHub paths and parent-titled MRs
description: Found by review of the reap forge search. (1) A remote using an SSH host alias (git@github-work:o/r.git) selects github with host github-work; gh has no login there, every search fails, and reap keeps every claim with no other evidence on every run, under a warning that blames the CLI login. (2) A GitHub remote with more than owner/repo in its path gives gh a --repo it rejects, with the same effect. (3) The title filter walks parent ids, so for a child claim a search hit titled with its epic or a sibling (bops-260 or bops-260.1 for bops-260.2) keeps the claim as that MR's work. (4) Any PR author can keep a claim by naming the bead in an open PR title; consider showing the MR author in the evidence.
acceptance_criteria: An SSH alias host or a nested GitHub path is reported as such (or resolved to the real host) rather than as a failed login; a child claim is not kept by an MR titled only with its parent's or sibling's id; tests use the fake forge.

title: bops reap: a merged merge request keeps a claim on every run
description: Since reap searches the forge, any merged MR whose title or branch carries a bead id (or, by the '.'-bounded match, a child's id such as <id>.1) keeps a stale claim on that bead forever: a bead reopened after an earlier MR merged, or an epic whose child MR merged, is never reapable, and --only does not override evidence. The only way out is --forge none or a hand claim --force. Fix: count a merged MR as evidence only when it merged after the claim was made (search merged_at / mergedAt against the claim time), and say in the kept detail how to release it.
acceptance_criteria: A stale claim on a bead whose only forge MR merged before the claim was made is released (or listed would_release); one merged after the claim is kept; the kept detail names how to override; tests use the fake forge.

title: bops reap: find merge requests that name a bead only in their branch, or name its parent
description: reap's forge search (gh pr list --search, GitLab search=) matches titles and descriptions only, so a merge request from a fork, or merged with its branch deleted, that names the bead only in its source branch is not found and the claim can be released. A child bead's search also does not find a merge request titled with its parent's id. Options: for GitHub, gh pr list --head <branch> for the branch the configured branch_pattern gives (exact match, not search-indexed); search ancestor ids too; batch the searches (one listing of recent MRs per run, matched locally) to stay under GitHub's ~30/min search rate limit.
acceptance_criteria: A stale claim whose only evidence is a forge MR whose source branch (not title or description) carries the bead id is kept; tests use the fake forge; the number of forge calls per reap run is stated and tested.

title: bops reap: a branch whose <id> the agent shortened or slugged is still invisible
description: branch_pattern now must carry a bounded <id>, but the agent fills the placeholder itself. A branch where it wrote a shortened, slugged or otherwise altered bead id holds pushed work that bops reap (BranchNamesBead) cannot see, so reap can still release that claim as holding none. Validating the pattern cannot catch this. Options: have bops land or doctor check that the current branch passes BranchNamesBead for the bead, and warn if not; or make the skill text say plainly that <id> is the bead id verbatim.
acceptance_criteria: A branch for a bead whose name does not carry the bead id as BranchNamesBead reads it is reported (land/doctor warning or equivalent), with a test; or the decision not to is recorded.

title: bops reap/release: a pending or partial local release can be published over a newer claim
description: Two gaps found reviewing the reap release-pending change. (1) A release written to the local ledger whose push failed stays as a local Dolt commit; if another machine takes the ref over meanwhile, finishRelease now drops the hold without pushing, but any later unrelated pushLedger from this clone still publishes that commit over the new holder's claim display (or conflicts on assignee/status). (2) releaseDisplay's bd writes (assignee/status, run label, bops:hold, comment) are not atomic: a failure part way leaves a half-release in the local ledger, which the next push from this clone publishes while the ref is still held; sync's re-display does not remove bops:hold.
acceptance_criteria: Decide how a moot or partial local release commit is undone or superseded before it is published; tests cover a takeover during the pending window and a releaseDisplay failure after its first write.

title: bops release: keep the claim ref until the release's ledger push lands, as reap now does
description: Plain bops release still deletes the claim ref when its ledger push fails (ledger_pending), so other machines see a remote ledger showing this run in progress with no ref, a claim a plain claim refuses, until sync from this clone pushes. reap now keeps the ref (journal release_pending) until the push lands; releaseLocked's keepRef path could be the default for every reason but done.
acceptance_criteria: A plain release whose ledger push fails keeps its claim ref, release pending, until sync or the next command on the bead pushes; a test covers it.

title: bops: conflict screen for claim --next and between candidates in one answer
description: next --avoid-conflicts screens candidates only against live claims. claim --next and the next_candidate hint after a lost claim call next without the screen, and two candidates in one next answer can overlap each other, so an orchestrator filling several slots from one answer can still dispatch colliding beads.
acceptance_criteria: claim --next takes --avoid-conflicts and passes it to next_candidate; with the flag, next marks a later workable candidate whose touches: overlap an earlier workable one in the same answer as unworkable, naming it in why_not; tests cover both; docs updated.

title: bops: scope op-id replay to the hold instance
description: A derived op id hashes command, bead, run and content, not the hold. After a run releases a bead, re-claims it in the same run, loses it to another run's claim --force, and then runs release with the same reason and text, release finds the first hold's bops:released comment and answers released/replayed instead of refused (not held). Likewise a note repeating an earlier hold's text is replayed (it still refreshes the claim). bops:claimed is written once per run, so comments alone cannot tell holds apart.
acceptance_criteria: A release or note replay matches only an op recorded during the current or most recent hold of this run; the release/re-claim/lose/release sequence answers refused; tests cover it.

title: bops lock: TestDoctorUnreachableRemote is flaky
description: TestDoctorUnreachableRemote in bops/internal/lock failed once during a full go test ./... run while bops-319 was being built, then passed on rerun and on main. The package was untouched. Find the timing or environment dependency and make the test deterministic.
acceptance_criteria: Root cause named; the test passes 50 consecutive runs with -count=50 under -race.

title: bops status: judge ref-only rows from the bead's status, and keep local branches offline
description: bops status reads only in-progress beads, so a claim ref whose bead is closed (a landing ref after raw bd close), blocked or deferred (a parked claim sync keeps) is judged from the ref alone: a closed bead's landing ref shows as landing, a parked claim as an orphan once idle. Branch inference is all or nothing: workBranches fails on the first ls-remote, and status skips it when the claim-ref fetch failed and under lock.mode none, though local refs and worktrees need no network. Comment reads are serial, one bd call per claim, inside the 60 s budget.
acceptance_criteria: status reads the bead status of ref-only rows (one bd call) and reports a closed bead's ref as closed and a blocked/deferred claim as parked; branch lookup keeps local branches when remotes fail and under lock.mode none; comment reads are bounded-concurrent or the board says when the budget cut it short; tests for each.

comments.author: Alex Nelson
comments.text: Also from review: when origin is a different, unreachable remote, workBranches' ls-remote calls (20 s each) can use most of status's 60 s budget before any comment is read. Give branch lookup its own sub-deadline or read comments first, and split workBranches into its network part (ls-remote) and local part (for-each-ref, worktree list) so offline still finds local branches. Also: a bead with several run: labels keys age/last note on runs[0] (stale does the same).

comments.author: Alex Nelson
comments.text: Also from review pass 3: on a ref row whose run has no bops:claimed comment, age_minutes falls back to the ledger claim's started_at, which may be another run's; a no-ref claim with a future ledger time (clock skew) shows live, not unknown (stale does the same); printKV top-level strings (reason, detail) are printed uncleaned.

title: bops claim --force previous.branch: keep a partial branch list, and clean warnings in text output
description: claim --force fills previous.branch from workBranches, which fails as a whole when any one ls-remote fails (e.g. origin unreachable while the lock remote answers), so local and last-fetch matches are lost too. Separately, warnings (now including git/bd error text from the handoff reads) print in text mode via printKV without cleanText, so multi-line stderr breaks key=value framing.
acceptance_criteria: A failed ls-remote on one remote warns and keeps the other listings for previous.branch; text-mode warnings pass through cleanText with newlines flattened; tests cover both.

title: bops human output: cleanText passes Unicode format characters (bidi overrides)
description: cleanText in bops/cmd/bops/commands.go replaces only unicode.IsControl (Cc) runes. Format characters (Cf) such as U+202E and U+2066-2069 pass through, so ledger text printed at a terminal (previous_last_note, reasons, details) can display differently from its bytes.
acceptance_criteria: cleanText also replaces Cf runes (at least the bidi controls); a test covers U+202E in human output.

title: bops claim --next: spread racing agents across candidates instead of one shared order
description: Every agent running bops claim --next walks next's candidates in the same deterministic order, so with k agents racing, agent k loses about k-1 races (one push each) and, with 6+ racers or several heads just taken, can hit the 5-try cap and answer refused while workable beads remain. The candidate list is computed once and not refreshed between tries. Options: re-run next (fresh fetch) after a loss, or rotate/jitter among candidates of equal priority per run. Found in review of the claim --next change.
acceptance_criteria: With N agents racing claim --next over at least N free beads, each gets a bead without hitting the try cap; tests cover a refresh or rotation between tries.

title: bops renew: batch ids in the MCP/clj bindings and read claim refs once
description: The manifest gives renew a single id, so MCP, Clojure and Hermes callers renew one bead per process call, each with its own state load and ls-remote, although the CLI and output take several. Each renewed bead also costs an ls-remote in checkHold before its leased push. Consider an ids: string[] argument mapped to positional ids in mcpArgv and the clj argv, and one ls-remote over this run's claim refs before the loop.
acceptance_criteria: An MCP or clj caller can renew several beads in one call; a renew of N beads makes one ref read before its pushes.

title: lock.Delete drops every run's journal entry for the id even when the delete lost
description: In bops/internal/lock/lock.go Delete, the lost path (the ref was found at another sha) calls Journal.Drop(id), which forgets the id for every run in the clone. Callers rely on the per-bead file lock to keep another worktree of the clone from claiming meanwhile, but lockBead returns a no-op unlock when the state directory has no file locks (ErrBeadLockUnsupported). Then a claim --force in another worktree can replace the ref between a sweep or gc read and its leased delete: the lease correctly refuses the delete, but Drop erases that run's fresh hold, so the clone forgets a claim it owns on the remote.
acceptance_criteria: Delete's lost path drops only a journal entry whose sha or intended sha equals the expected sha (compare-and-drop); a test shows a fresh hold of another run survives a lost delete.

title: check-bindings.sh: fail on checked-in binding files the generator no longer writes
description: scripts/check-bindings.sh walks only the files bops gen produces. A conditionally generated file (bindings/claude-code/guard-hooks.json is written only while a command lists hook:PreToolUse) would go stale if the surface were removed, and CI would stay green. Compare listings both ways, excluding hand-written files (README.md, CLAUDE.md.snippet, settings.json).
acceptance_criteria: check-bindings.sh fails when a binding directory holds a generated-looking file the generator did not write; hand-written files are allow-listed; tested by removing a surface in a temp copy.

title: bops guard: check scripts fed to a shell on stdin, and shell tools other than Bash
description: bops guard skips heredoc bodies, so `bash <<'EOF'\nbd reclaim\nEOF` and `sh -s <<EOF` are allowed, and the PreToolUse matcher is Bash only, so a raw claim sent through another tool that runs shell commands (e.g. Monitor) never reaches it. Proposal: keep heredoc bodies tied to their command and check() the body when the command word is a shell with no -c; consider widening the matcher (Bash|Monitor) and accepting those tool_names when tool_input.command is present. Both are false negatives only (the guard fails open by design).
acceptance_criteria: bash <<EOF and sh -s <<EOF bodies containing bd reclaim are refused on a lock-on ledger; a decision recorded (and tested) on which tool names the hook covers; tests for each.

title: bops reap: ask the forge for PRs naming the bead before releasing
description:
`bops reap` looks for branches only on the lock remote, origin and this clone. A PR opened from a fork or another remote, or a PR merged with its branch auto-deleted after an agent died between opening it and `bops land` recording it, leaves no evidence, so reap releases the claim and the work may be redone.

Proposal: ask the forge for open or merged PRs/MRs naming the bead id (the forge adapter sweep uses could gain a search call), and treat any as evidence. Weigh the cost of one forge call per stale claim against the budget.

Raised by the adversarial pass of the bops-n71 review.
acceptance_criteria: A stale claim whose bead id appears in an open or merged PR/MR title or branch on the forge is kept with that PR as evidence; a forge failure keeps the claim; tests use the fake forge.

title: bops reap: branch evidence is invisible when branch_pattern does not carry the bead id
description:
`bops reap` finds branch evidence only when a branch name carries the bead id (or its suffix, or a parent's) as a token. `validBranchPattern` (bops/internal/config/branch.go) accepts a `branch_pattern` with no `<id>`, such as `feat/<slug>`, or with `<id>` not bounded by a separator. In such a repo, pushed work with no MR recorded yet is invisible to reap, and the claim is released as having no work.

Options: require `<id>`, bounded by a separator or the ends, in `branch_pattern`; or have reap read the configured pattern and warn (or refuse to release) when it cannot carry the id.

Raised by the adversarial pass of the bops-n71 review.
acceptance_criteria: Either branch_pattern requires a bounded <id> (config tests cover it) or reap warns/refuses for a pattern that cannot carry the id (reap test covers it).

title: bops reap: take over and release under one bead lock, deleting the ref only after the ledger push
description:
`bops reap` takes a stale claim over with `claim --force`, then gives it back with `release --reason abandoned`, as two separate commands, each under its own per-bead lock. In between, a concurrent `bops sync` or session-start in the same clone (same run) can act on the fresh hold. Worse: if the takeover's ledger push fails (ledger_pending) and the release's push fails too, the release has already deleted the claim ref on the remote while the remote ledger still shows the original holder in_progress with its run: label. Other machines then see a ledger-only claim that a plain claim refuses, until someone runs `bops sync` from the reaping clone.

Proposal: an internal takeover-and-release path that holds one bead lock for both steps, and deletes the claim ref only after the release's ledger push has landed (or keeps the hold with ledger_pending so sync re-drives the release).

Found by the red-team pass of the bops-n71 review.
acceptance_criteria: A reap whose takeover and release ledger pushes both fail leaves no state where the ref is gone but the remote ledger still shows the old holder; a test covers it; sync cannot act between the two steps.

title: bops: reduce ledger push contention structurally
description:
Every claim, land, release and sync pushes the shared Dolt ledger ref, so concurrent writers on several machines meet non-fast-forward rejections; retries make it survivable but not cheap.

title: bops: fencing token so a superseded holder cannot write after a takeover
description:
After `bops claim --force` takes over a stale claim, the original holder may revive (a suspended machine, a slow agent). Lock literature calls a lock without fencing only an efficiency lock: a paused holder resumes and writes with an outdated grant (https://oneuptime.com/blog/post/2026-09-09-etcd-fenced-lock-leases-revisions/view). Retasc issues a fencing token per claim and rejects writes from older tokens.

Verify first: bops may already answer `lost` on note/land/release when the ref names another run. If so, this bead narrows to making the generation explicit and tested.
acceptance_criteria: Each claim carries a monotonically increasing generation stored in or beside the lock ref; note, land and release check it and answer lost when a later claim (e.g. claim --force) superseded the caller; test: a holder whose claim was forced cannot land. First confirm what bops already checks today and record it on this bead.

bops:note run=01M8DVB2H5VN8ZY7THTFVPJ6N6 op=d-06e571cc2fc3091e
What bops checks today (verified in code): every claim ref write commits a fresh commit with a random 16-byte nonce, and the run's journal (runstate Held[id].SHA) records the sha it last confirmed. note (refreshRef -> checkHold), land (checkHold) and release (verifyHold) all re-read the live ref and Settle it against the journal: any other sha is Displaced -> the hold is dropped and the command answers lost with the holder. claim --force replaces the ref with a new commit (lease on the sha it read), so the superseded holder already answers lost on land/release, and on note when the remote is reachable (note writes offline by design when the ref cannot be read). So the sha is already a fencing token (unique, never reused); what is missing is an explicit, ordered generation and tests naming the forced-holder case for land.

Known limits kept: a legacy hold (no sha, pre-lock) and lock.mode none have no ref to fence; the check and the ledger write are not atomic (bd has no CAS), so a takeover in that window is caught at the next command.

KEY DECISION: add gen=<n> to the claim ref message (an extra key; older bops ignore unknown keys, a ref with no gen reads as 0 = unrecorded, so contract stays 1). Acquire writes gen=1; a Replace by the same run (refresh, landing) keeps the gen; a Replace by another run (claim --force, claim --resume) writes the expected ref's gen+1. The gen of the expected ref is read from its local commit object (Read fetched it; own commits are local). The fence stays the sha compare (strictly stronger); the generation is reported on lost answers (holder.generation) and on claim (generation), so a superseded holder sees which later claim won. Generations count within one ref's life; a delete ends every hold.

title: Beads pre-commit hook commits a stale issues.jsonl export
description:
Committing .beads/issues.jsonl by hand sometimes records a stale export. Seen three times on 2026-11-11 (bd 1.3.4, Homebrew), each time on plan/bops-v0.1.0-ceo-review:

1. eafb6bc: the commit printed "Exported 38 issues"; afterwards issues.jsonl was modified again by one line (bops-4lv open -> in_progress, the claim made just before).
2. 0cb63b3: ran `bd export` explicitly, then `git add` + `git commit`; the hook printed "Exported 43 issues" and the committed file had bops-ecs `open` (updated_at 18:13:09Z) while the ledger had it `in_progress` (18:13:10Z, claimed a second later in the same command sequence). Fixed by 2d91670, committed with --no-verify.
3. Earlier (19273b4 era) the same one-line drift after a claim.

In every case the drift is the most recent write to the ledger (a claim), and the pre-commit hook (core.hooksPath=.beads/hooks, pre-commit -> `bd hooks run pre-commit`, BEADS INTEGRATION v1.3.4) re-exports during the commit. Hypotheses to test: the hook exports from a stale read (incremental export keyed on .beads/export-state.json, or a Dolt working set vs committed state), or it exports to the worktree after the index was staged so the commit keeps the older staged copy while the worktree gets the newer one.

Note: the hook also fires from agent worktrees and writes the MAIN checkout's .beads/issues.jsonl (a subagent reported "Exported 38 issues to /Users/.../beads-ops/.beads/issues.jsonl" while committing in .claude/worktrees/agent-*).
acceptance_criteria: Root cause identified with a reproduction (claim a bead, then commit issues.jsonl, then compare committed vs bd export output); either a fix or config here so a commit records the current ledger, or an upstream beads issue drafted for the owner to review (nothing posted without approval); PROCESS.md says how to commit the export safely meanwhile.

title: Report a missing Dolt remote in lock.mode ref from doctor and sync
description: Found in bops-b5c (PR #13). Claims in ref mode now refuse with remote_mismatch when there is no Dolt remote, but release, land, sweep and sync don't call checkRemote. In ref mode with no Dolt remote (a claim made before #13, or the Dolt remote removed later): sync and sweep fail at bd dolt pull ('no remote', exit 1); release deletes the ref then leaves the ledger pending with a warning; land succeeds silently because bd dolt push exits 0 'skipping'. Have doctor (which today never reads the Dolt remote list) and sync report the missing Dolt remote with the same fix advice as remote_mismatch, and decide whether land should warn.
acceptance_criteria: In ref mode with no Dolt remote, bops doctor reports a failing check naming the missing Dolt remote with both fixes (add a Dolt remote, or lock.mode none in .bops.json); sync's error or warning names the cause instead of the raw bd error; land warns that the ledger was not published; tests cover each; lock.mode none is unaffected.

title: Refuse claims in lock.mode ref when no Dolt remote exists
description: Found while doing bops-q85 (PR #12). In lock.mode ref, checkRemote returns nil when the Dolt remote list is empty, so a repo with a git origin but no Dolt remote passes the remote check. The claim lock then runs with no ledger remote beside it, contrary to the design rule that the lock must live beside the ledger (SPEC §3.0, design doc 'the lock must live beside the ledger'); sync and claim --force only fail later at the publish step. Under lock.mode none this case is handled by q85's 'no Dolt remote: ledger not published' skip.
acceptance_criteria: In lock.mode ref with a git lock remote and an empty Dolt remote list, claim (and claim --force) refuse before any ref push with a stable code (reuse remote_mismatch, or justify a new one in SPEC); lock.mode none is unaffected; a test covers both modes; SPEC's stable-code text says so.

title: Infer the forge from lock.remote instead of origin
description: bops/internal/forge/forge.go infers the forge from 'git remote get-url origin'. acceptance_criteria: With lock.remote set to a non-origin remote and no forge config, forge inference reads that remote; a test covers it; SPEC's forge-selection sentence is updated.

title: Treat no Dolt remote as nothing to publish under lock.mode none

comments.author: Alex Nelson
comments.text:
Thanks for writing this up. We hit the same race and can add some data, plus the workaround we built in the meantime.

**What we observed (bd 1.3.4)**

In a two-replica test (two clones, one git remote) we ran `bd update <id> --claim` on both replicas at once. Both claims succeeded locally. A's `bd dolt push` succeeded and B's was rejected. B then ran `bd dolt pull`, Dolt settled `assignee` last-write-wins in B's favour, and B pushed. This happened in both of the runs we did. Both replicas were on one machine, so this shows the race exists, not how often it happens on a real network.

Your report mentions the notices that `pull` prints. In our sequence the side that pulls is the side that wins, so the notice goes to the winner. The replica that was told its claim succeeded (A) never pulls a conflict and is never told it lost. `--if-assignee` / `--if-status` don't help, because they compare and set on one replica too, and `bd update --claim` refuses to combine with them.

**Workaround: a git-ref claim lock** ([design](https://github.com/extremenelson/beads-ops/blob/3a9f2bc81312d7cdcffe5c73ab8b5013971ee7d9/docs/designs/bops-claim-lock-v0.1.0.md), [ADR amendment](https://github.com/extremenelson/beads-ops/blob/3a9f2bc81312d7cdcffe5c73ab8b5013971ee7d9/docs/adr/0001-derived-read-model-not-write-path.md#amendment-2026-11-10-a-git-ref-claim-lock))

Each bead gets one ref, `refs/bops/claims/<id>`, on the same remote as `refs/dolt/data`. It is written with `git push --force-with-lease=<ref>:<expected>` (an empty `<expected>` for a create-only push), so the forge's ref update is the compare-and-set. Exactly one machine wins. The loser exits non-zero before touching the ledger. The ref holds only run, actor, state, nonce and timestamp, never issue data, and `bd update --claim` is still written afterwards so people and tools that read the ledger can see who holds the bead.

Measured:
- Raw git on GitHub, two clones pushing at once: exactly one winner in 40 of 40 create-only races and 20 of 20 leased-replace (takeover) races ([results](https://github.com/extremenelson/beads-ops/blob/3a9f2bc81312d7cdcffe5c73ab8b5013971ee7d9/bops/testdata/README.md#git-ref-lock-on-github-git-2560-2026-11-09)).
- End to end against real bd 1.3.4 in CI (two clones, a local bare remote, one runner): 40 races with distinct actors and 40 with one shared actor. Every trial ended with exactly one `claimed` and one `lost`. Claim latency was p50 2.26 s / max 4.33 s and p50 2.02 s / max 2.66 s respectively ([test](https://github.com/extremenelson/beads-ops/blob/3a9f2bc81312d7cdcffe5c73ab8b5013971ee7d9/bops/cmd/bops/replica_test.go), [CI run](https://github.com/extremenelson/beads-ops/actions/runs/42954571258)). Forty clean trials only bound the failure rate to roughly 7.5% at 95% confidence. The guarantee rests on the server's leased push, not on the trial count.

Costs:
- It is a second write path just for ownership, and it covers only claims made through our wrapper. A raw `bd update --claim` bypasses it.
- A claim now needs the network. Offline claims are refused.
- It needs a forge that accepts custom refs with `--force-with-lease`. We have only measured GitHub.
- Each lock commit needs a nonce. Pushing an identical object reports success to both sides.
- About 2 s per claim in our CI.

We plan to delete the lock the day bd can do this itself.

**The ask**

A cross-replica compare-and-set on claim: a `bd update --claim` (or `bd ready --claim`) that, when a remote is configured, either wins against the remote or fails with a distinct exit code, instead of succeeding locally and being settled last-write-wins later.

If that doesn't fit the Dolt model, any one of these would let tools build it without a side channel:
1. A conditional push: `bd dolt push` that refuses, rather than merging, when a named cell (here `assignee`) changed on the remote since the local base.
2. A machine-readable report from `bd dolt pull` of which local writes lost last-write-wins (issue id, field, local and winning values), so the loser can be told.
3. Confirmation that the `expectedRevision` compare-and-swap on the ROADMAP (#6136) will be checked against the remote and not only the local replica, which would cover this.

Happy to test a branch against the suite above.

title: bops reap: let --only pin the holder the preview showed (id@run)
description:
`bops reap --only <id>,<id>` names beads, not holders. If another person force-takes one of the previewed claims between the preview and the real run, and then goes idle past the window, the real run releases a different holder's claim than the one the operator saw.

Proposal: accept `<id>@<run>` in --only (the preview prints each claim's run), and release only when the stale claim's run still matches; a bare id keeps today's behaviour.

Raised by the adversarial pass of the bops-n71 review.
acceptance_criteria: --only accepts <id>@<run>; a claim whose run no longer matches is listed under skipped, not released; a bare id behaves as before; tests cover both.

title: bops reap: reuse the comments and issue Stale already read
description:
`bops reap` calls `Stale`, which already runs `bd comments` for ledger-sourced and cross-machine stale claims, then `workEvidence` runs `bd show` and `bd comments` again for every claim (and a real run does it twice more per claim, before and after the takeover). Each call opens Dolt (about 0.3-1 s), so a 30-claim run spends tens of seconds of its 5-minute budget re-reading data it already had.

Proposal: carry the comments (and the issue) Stale decoded on StaleClaim and reuse them for the first evidence read; keep the fresh reads only where staleness matters (just before and after the takeover).

Found by the performance pass of the bops-n71 review.
acceptance_criteria: reap makes no bd comments or bd show call for a claim whose data Stale already decoded, except the fresh reads just before and after a takeover; a test counts the calls.

KEY DECISION: StaleClaim carries the decoded issue and comments (unexported); the first evidence read reuses them until this run has attempted a takeover (whose pull may bring newer ledger data), then reads fresh. The post-takeover read in reapOne is unchanged. Tests count show/comments calls (dry and real) and cover the fresh read after a takeover.
